headline: Draft policy prohibiting smart glasses and wearable recording devices in schools, and the meeting schedule.
summary: The subcommittee will review a draft policy that prohibits smart glasses and wearable recording devices on school property, with some exceptions. It will also discuss the meeting schedule.
items: Smart Glasses Policy: draft policy prohibiting smart glasses and wearable recording devices on school property

DRAFT
 
Salem
 
Public
 
Schools’
 
Policy
 
Prohibiting
 
Smart
 
Glasses
 
and
 
Wearable
 
Recording
 
Devices
 
 
1.
 
Purpose
 
The
 
Salem
 
Public
 
School
 
District
 
(the
 
“District”)
 
acknowledges
 
that
 
technology
 
is
 
an
 
increasingly
 
common
 
part
 
of
 
everyday
 
life,
 
including
 
in
 
schools.
 
However,
 
devices
 
that
 
can
 
record
 
audio
 
or
 
video
 
discreetly
 
raise
 
concerns
 
about
 
student
 
privacy,
 
classroom
 
distractions,
 
and
 
academic
 
integrity.
 
 
The
 
District
 
is
 
committed
 
to
 
maintaining
 
a
 
safe,
 
respectful,
 
and
 
focused
 
learning
 
environment
 
where
 
technology
 
represents
 
a
 
healthy
 
and
 
constructive
 
aspect
 
of
 
students’
 
lives.
 
The
 
District
 
recognizes
 
the
 
importance
 
of
 
building
 
strong
 
relationships
 
among
 
students
 
and
 
educators
 
and
 
promoting
 
healthy
 
technology
 
habits.
 
 
To
 
protect
 
student
 
and
 
staff
 
privacy
 
and
 
support
 
learning,
 
the
 
District
 
prohibits
 
the
 
possession
 
and
 
use
 
of
 
smart
 
glasses
 
and
 
other
 
wearable
 
recording
 
devices
 
on
 
school
 
property,
 
except
 
as
 
expressly
 
authorized
 
under
 
this
 
policy.
 
 
This
 
policy
 
is
 
specifically
 
designed
 
to:
 
●
 
Increase
 
student
 
engagement
 
in
 
the
 
classroom.
 
●
 
Reduce
 
distractions
 
from
 
non-academic
 
notifications
 
and
 
content.
 
●
 
Prevent
 
the
 
recording
 
of
 
peers
 
or
 
staff
 
without
 
a
 
second
 
party’s
 
consent.
 
●
 
Decrease
 
incidents
 
of
 
cyberbullying
 
and
 
inappropriate
 
social
 
media
 
use.
 
●
 
Encourage
 
students
 
to
 
build
 
stronger
 
interpersonal
 
relationships
 
with
 
peers
 
and
 
staff.
 
●
 
Preserve
 
the
 
integrity
 
of
 
in-class
 
examinations,
 
quizzes,
 
assignments
 
or
 
other
 
academic
 
activities.
 
 
2.
 
Definitions
 
Wearable
 
technology
 
means
 
electronic
 
devices
 
worn
 
on
 
the
 
body
 
that
 
can
 
capture,
 
record,
 
or
 
transmit
 
audio,
 
video,
 
or
 
images.
 
 
Prohibited
 
devices
 
include,
 
but
 
are
 
not
 
limited
 
to:
 
●
 
Smart
 
glasses,
 
including
 
Meta
 
smart
 
glasses
 
and
 
similar
 
devices
 
with
 
recording
 
capabilities.
 
●
 
Smartwatches
 
or
 
other
 
wearable
 
devices
 
with
 
audio
 
or
 
video
 
recording
 
capabilities.
 
●
 
Wearable
 
AI
 
voice
 
recorders,
 
recording
 
pins,
 
and
 
similar
 
devices.
 
●
 
Other
 
wearable
 
devices
 
capable
 
of
 
covertly
 
recording
 
audio,
 
video,
 
or
 
images.
 
 
The
 
prohibition
 
applies
 
regardless
 
of
 
whether
 
a
 
device
 
is
 
actively
 
recording
 
or
 
whether
 
its
 
recording
 
functions
 
are
 
visible.
 
 
3.
 
Prohibition
 
Students
 
may
 
not
 
possess,
 
wear,
 
use,
 
or
 
operate
 
prohibited
 
devices
 
on
 
District
 
school
 
property.
 
This
 
prohibition
 
applies
 
to
 
all
 
District
 
schools
 
and
 
school
 
property,
 
including
 
classrooms,
DRAFT
 
hallways,
 
cafeterias,
 
school
 
grounds,
 
and
 
school
 
buses.
 
It
 
also
 
applies
 
during
 
school-sponsored
 
activities
 
and
 
events
 
held
 
on
 
or
 
off
 
school
 
property.
 
 
The
 
prohibition
 
applies
 
throughout
 
the
 
school
 
day,
 
including
 
before
 
and
 
after
 
school
 
when
 
students
 
are
 
participating
 
in
 
school
 
activities.
 
 
4.
 
Exceptions
 
The
 
District
 
recognizes
 
that
 
wearable
 
technology
 
may,
 
in
 
some
 
circumstances,
 
support
 
a
 
student’s
 
learning
 
or
 
accessibility
 
needs.
 
 
A
 
student
 
may
 
use
 
a
 
prohibited
 
device
 
only
 
when
 
expressly
 
authorized
 
in
 
writing
 
by
 
the
 
Superintendent
 
for
 
a
 
documented
 
educational,
 
disability-related
 
approved
 
purpose.
 
Any
 
authorization
 
must
 
specify
 
the
 
permitted
 
device,
 
purpose,
 
and
 
conditions
 
of
 
use.
 
 
The
 
District
 
will
 
consider
 
appropriate
 
accommodations
 
for
 
students
 
with
 
disabilities
 
in
 
accordance
 
with
 
applicable
 
law.
 
 
5.
 
Enforcement
 
School
 
administrators
 
are
 
responsible
 
for
 
implementing
 
and
 
enforcing
 
this
 
policy.
 
Students
 
who
 
violate
 
the
 
policy
 
may
 
be
 
subject
 
to
 
appropriate
 
school
 
disciplinary
 
procedures
 
consistent
 
with
 
the
 
District’s
 
existing
 
policies
 
and
 
applicable
 
law.
 
 
School
 
administrators
 
may
 
direct
 
a
 
student
 
to
 
stop
 
using
 
a
 
prohibited
 
device
 
and
 
follow
 
school
 
procedures
 
for
 
addressing
 
the
 
violation.
 
 
6.
 
Scope
 
and
 
Review
 
This
 
policy
 
applies
 
to
 
all
 
students
 
across
 
the
 
District,
 
including
 
elementary,
 
middle,
 
and
 
high
 
school
 
students.
 
 
The
 
District
 
may
 
review
 
and
 
update
 
this
 
policy
 
as
 
technology
 
evolves
 
and
 
new
 
educational
 
needs
 
arise.
